headline: Spelling out the Progressive creed
summary: Privately, Roosevelt tells Victor Murdock he will not run in 1916 under either party. A Century Magazine article lays out the Progressive aims, arguing neither old party serves ordinary people. In Albany, Governor Sulzer is removed after his impeachment trial.

letters.topic: The 1916 nomination; privately will not run

tr_quotes.text: The problems connected with the trusts . . . child labor, and all similar matters can be solved only by affirmative national action. No party is progressive which does not set the authority of the national government as supreme in these matters. No party is progressive which does not give the people the right to determine for themselves . . . what the standards of social and industrial justice shall be . . . This is a government of the people, to be used for the people, so as to better the condition of the average man and average woman of the nation...

works.title: Century Magazine article on the Progressive Party
